findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_daily_content, get_pricing, latest_content · Private data: lookup_precedent, lookup_statute, bar_exam_search, get_exam_answer, get_daily_content, list_document_types, generate_document, find_village_lawyer, get_pricing, get_account · Public sink: get_daily_content, latest_content · Destructive: get_exam_answer, get_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_daily_content, get_pricing, latest_content · Private data: lookup_precedent, lookup_statute, bar_exam_search, get_exam_answer, get_daily_content, list_document_types, generate_document, find_village_lawyer, get_pricing, get_account · Public sink: get_daily_content, latest_content · Destructive: get_exam_answer, get_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "lookup_precedent" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
